solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Score and enter hit parade this year?

parts.note: a score is a count of twenty

indicators.note: to parade troops is to march them about, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A cheerful invitation to get into the charts this year.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared at the turn of the year, so 'this year' points at the new year's number; 'hit parade' looks like the charts but 'parade' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The year in which the puzzle was published, written out in words as a number.

clue.text: A selection of gateaus! I'm a ritualist over 21!

definitions.note: the solution to 21 Down, a dessert course

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the letters are read upwards, backwards
a selection is a run of letters taken from the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone choosing cakes declares themselves a devotee of ritual over dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: The run USIMARIT, from the end of 'gateaus' through the start of 'ritualist', is read backwards because of 'over'.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian coffee-flavoured dessert is an example of a pudding.

clue.text: Head off hack, maybe, undermining objective advocate

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece going under another puts it after that piece

parts.note: an objective is an end or aim

indicators.note: taking the head off removes the first letter

parts.note: a hack is a riding horse, so this is a horse

explanation.surface: A journalist undermining an impartial supporter of a cause, with someone told to head him off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hack' looks like a journalist, but it is the riding horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate a course is to support or back it publicly, a synonym.

clue.text: Couple's handwriting editor finds clumsy

parts.note: a couple is two
fist is an informal word for a person's handwriting

explanation.surface: An editor complains that a pair of writers have awkward handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone heavy-handed and awkward is described as having two fists, a synonym for clumsy.

clue.text: See 1
When pushed, he and I mug up angina as experimental subject

indicators.note: pushed around, the letters are shoved into a new order

explanation.surface: Two people swot up on heart pain when pressed to do so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the two parts of the anagram fodder: HE plus I MUG UP ANGINA.
explanation.definitionFit: A person used as the subject of a trial or test is an idiomatic version of the laboratory animal.

clue.text: Bring back Descartes Week!

parts.note: René Descartes was the French philosopher

explanation.surface: A call to revive a week celebrating the French philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore or revive something is to bring it back, a synonym.

clue.text: Potential for being, say, good on film?

parts.note: EG, for example, is signalled by say
a cel or cell is a transparent celluloid sheet used in animated film

explanation.surface: A question whether someone would come across well on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply places the film piece after the others in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A female reproductive cell is a life not yet begun, potentially a new living creature.

clue.text: 13 gathers books on Arabia for lawyer

indicators.note: one piece gathering others holds them inside it

parts.note: 13 Across is the new year, abbreviated to its initials
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A season gathers books about Arabia for a legal professional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link here: the books and Arabia both go inside NY.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal officer who witnesses and certifies documents is a kind of lawyer.

clue.text: Singing in the abbey, received constant upset with Scot's crack about top note

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the pieces upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: Roger is radio-speak for message received
G is the gravitational constant
Ian is a typical Scottish first name

indicators.note: one piece about another goes around it

parts.note: crack, or craic, is chat or banter

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Plainsong in the abbey is disrupted by a Scotsman's wisecrack about a high note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scot's crack' reads as one idea but splits into two pieces; 'received' is radio-speak, and 'upset' turns the first two pieces upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaccompanied liturgical plainsong of the Western church is what monks would sing in an abbey.

clue.text: Player King's brief farewell accorded little weight

parts.note: R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king

indicators.note: brief means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: adios is Spanish for goodbye
a gram is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A monarch's curt goodbye is given little importance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' is a record player, not a sportsman or actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A combined radio and record player in one cabinet is a piece of furniture that plays music.

clue.text: Activity in the dark close to ending in embarrassment? …

parts.note: nigh means near or close

indicators.note: the ending in a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Something done in darkness nearly ends in embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: This leads into the next clue: the 'night' out on New Year's Eve gives way to the following day.
explanation.definitionFit: A night out is an evening's partying, an activity that takes place after dark.

clue.text: … Ineluctable consequence of the 11 before a new start for tippler — reforming's in order (today!)

indicators.note: putting letters in order rearranges them
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A drinker's hangover after a night out leads to resolutions to reform, on the first day of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforming' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'in order' does the rearranging. '(today!)' notes the puzzle appeared on New Year's Day.
explanation.definitionFit: The time after a night of heavy drinking, with its hangover, is an unavoidable result of the party.

clue.text: See 20
Stretch rope

definitions.meaning: an expanse, as of water or ice spread out
a sailing rope controlling the angle of a sail

explanation.definitionFit: A broad expanse of ice is so called, and so is a line used to trim a sail.

clue.text: Number in Lourdes having slipped discs

indicators.note: one piece placed in another goes inside it
letters that have slipped have moved out of their places

explanation.surface: Many pilgrims to Lourdes have slipped discs, hoping for a cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having slipped' rearranges Lourdes, and N is placed inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Small circular emblems or decorative plates are discs, a synonym.

clue.text: After endless dampness, use dry heat to do this?

definitions.text: After endless dampness, use dry heat to do this?

indicators.note: endless removes the final letter

parts.note: dew is the dampness that settles overnight

indicators.note: to use letters here is to work them into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice on how to dry something out once the moisture has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the reworked DRY HEAT after DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Using dry heat to remove water from something is precisely to dry it out completely.

clue.text: '13 tum' Pam gets help for monitoring?

indicators.note: gets, as in gets round, signals a rearrangement of the letters

parts.note: 13 Across is the new year, abbreviated to its initials

explanation.surface: Pam needs help keeping an eye on her new-year waistline.
explanation.definitionFit: The eardrum lets us hear, an aid to keeping track of sounds around us.

clue.text: Precipitate a Channel Islands evacuation?

parts.note: a drain is a draining, an emptying out

explanation.surface: A question whether to hurry an emptying of Jersey and Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precipitate' looks like a verb meaning hasten; it is a noun, something falling out of the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Polluted rainfall is a form of precipitation, what falls out of the atmosphere.

clue.text: Chatroom regularly offered cash for 'colourful' stuff

indicators.note: taken regularly means every other letter

parts.note: tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone in an online chat room was paid for posting lurid material.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange pigment found in carrots, a substance that gives colour.

clue.text: Cheerful little fellow we yearn to assign as 'Best in 1 Across 4!'

parts.note: Happy is one of the seven dwarfs in Snow White

indicators.note: to assign is to allot afresh, so the letters are dealt out in a new order

explanation.surface: A cheerful dwarf, longing to award a prize for the year's best.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Best' is a good wish for the year rather than a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional greeting wishes someone the best for the coming twelve months.

clue.text: Club one may join if 12 26 treatment fails?

definitions.text: Club one may join if 12 26 treatment fails?

parts.words: Club one may join if 12 26 treatment fails?
parts.note: being in the club is British slang for pregnant; the emergency contraceptive pill is named after the day after a night out

explanation.walkthrough: 'in the pudding club' is British slang for pregnant, the outcome if an emergency contraceptive does not work.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being pregnant uses this word to name the club one has joined.

clue.text: Succeeded earlier in 'Mastermind'

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
avant is French for before

explanation.surface: Someone won an earlier series of the television quiz.
explanation.walkthrough: Mastermind is a long-running BBC quiz show, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of great learning or intellect, a genius or expert.

clue.text: Paint Mr Cooper — short and carrying blubber

indicators.note: carrying another piece holds it inside
short means missing its final letter

parts.note: Alice Cooper is the American shock-rock singer
to blubber is to cry

explanation.surface: Painting a portrait of a short singer who is overweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blubber' looks like fat but is the verb to weep.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick-drying synthetic emulsion is a kind of paint.

clue.text: Poem wonderfully rich in content

indicators.note: the content of words is what they hold inside

explanation.surface: A poem whose content is wonderfully rich.
explanation.definitionFit: A short poem expressing personal feeling, or song words, is a kind of verse.

clue.text: 4 and 4 making twenty-six? How?

parts.note: 4 Across is thirteen, and two thirteens summed make twenty-six; 'How?' asks whether it makes sense

explanation.walkthrough: 4 Across is THIRTEEN, so two of them totalled give twenty-six; the phrase also means 'made sense'.
explanation.definitionFit: Two numbers that have been summed, and an idiom for something that made logical sense.

clue.text: See 12
Distress of American soldier, first on base to fail

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter
failing means dropping out of the word

parts.note: a station is a base, as a military post

explanation.surface: An American soldier is distressed when the first assault on the base fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' and 'to fail' together drop the opening S of STATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxiety or mental disturbance is a synonym for distress.

clue.text: Eat tiny bit of chocolate — breaking resolution!

indicators.note: breaking the letters smashes them into a new order
a bit of a word is here its first letter

explanation.surface: A dieter's New Year resolution is broken by eating a small piece of chocolate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolution' looks like a New Year pledge but is the definition, meaning determination.
explanation.definitionFit: Determination or persistence in pursuing a goal, a sense of the defining word.

clue.text: Eucalyptus found in wine put clock back

parts.note: red is red wine

indicators.note: putting a word back reads it in reverse

parts.note: clock is slang for face, and so is mug

explanation.surface: A tree found in a wine region, where clocks went back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put clock back' looks like the end of daylight saving; 'clock' means face.
explanation.definitionFit: An Australian species of eucalyptus tree with red timber or sap.
